Lessons.Title: Describing Distributions
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Describe (orally and in writing) various distributions as skewed, symmetric, or bell-shaped. Recall how to interpret (orally and in writing) the standard deviation as a measure of variability.

Describe a quantitative distribution by shape (symmetric, bell-like, skewed), center and spread. Standard deviation measures typical deviation around the mean in squared-distance units after square root. Extreme values can inflate it.

Source activity 4.1: Which One Doesn't Belong: Cracking Glass: Four different kinds of glass are hit with a hammer and the length of the longest crack formed is recorded. The process is repeated 150 times for each type of glass. Which one doesn’t belong? Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
